zh: 为了铺垫一下，这个核心理念是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the high-level idea here?
zh: 这里的高层级概念是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just like you, I've spent my whole career just really passionate about startups, figuring out how to build products that win, that emerge in new markets, and one of the things that I have learned over time or one of the things you hear a lot from a lot of folks is, to win, you have to really build a great product.
zh: 像你一样，我整个职业生涯都充满激情地致力于初创企业，探索如何构建获胜的产品，如何在新市场中涌现，而我随着时间的段学到的一件事，或者你从很多人那里听到的一件事是，要获胜，你必须真正构建一个很棒的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of advice boils down to that.
zh: 很多建议都归结为这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things that I feel like I've banged my head against the wall in a lot of ways in my career is actually telling people that building a great product is one of those things that's necessary, but not sufficient, and actually the separation is between those that build really great distribution.
zh: 在我职业生涯的很多方面，我觉得我一直在碰壁的一件事实际上是告诉人们，构建很棒的产品是必要的事情之一，但不是充分的，而真正的区别在于那些真正构建了很棒的渠道的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this general partner, his name's Alex Rampell, he's at Andreessen Horowitz, actually wrote this blog post 10 years ago back in I think 2015.
zh: 所以这位普通合伙人，他的名字叫 Alex Rampell，他在 Andreessen Horowitz，实际上在 10 年前写了一篇博客文章，我想是在 2015 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the essence of the blog post, he basically says one thing, which is that startups is a game of trying to get distribution before the incumbent can copy.
zh: 在这篇博客文章的精髓中，他基本上说了一件事，那就是初创企业是一场试图在现有企业复制之前获得渠道的游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's this kind of concept of escape philosophy.
zh: 这是这种逃离哲学的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: On that note, which I think os a very good summary of what you're trying to do in a startup and distribution, is that we're right now living in this environment where that game of startups getting distribution faster than the incumbent has gotten way harder in a lot of ways, and in some small cases has gotten a little bit easier.
zh: 关于这一点，我认为这是对你试图在初创企业和渠道中做的事情的一个很好的总结，是我们现在正生活在这个环境中，初创企业比现有企业更快获得渠道的游戏在许多方面变得更难了，在一些极少数情况下变得稍微容易了一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if we think about this, the way that it's gotten harder and some of the things that probably a lot of founders or folks working on the growth side that probably feel is that, one is that incumbents can copy faster these days.
zh: 但如果我们思考这一点，它变得更难的方式，以及很多创始人或从事增长工作的人可能感受到的一些事情是，一是现有企业现在复制得更快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That window that you have to get that escape velocity has actually shrunk.
zh: 你获得那种逃逸速度的窗口实际上已经缩小了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's decreased.
zh: 它减少了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing is that a lot of the organic distribution that we've had, especially over the past few years, has really shrunk as well.
zh: 第二件事是，我们拥有的很多自然渠道，尤其是在过去几年里，也真正缩小了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody's talking about the decline of SEO and clicks declining, but you also see it in some other cases.
zh: 每个人都在谈论 SEO 的衰落和点击量的下降，但在一些其他情况下你也看到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of these social platforms don't really let you send as much traffic to sites.
zh: 许多这些社交平台并不真的让你向网站发送那么多流量。

speaker: Unknown
en: LinkedIn just changed their algorithm, which has really dropped organic distribution.
zh: LinkedIn 刚刚改变了他们的算法，这真的使得自然分布下降了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously the Twitter-to-X, transition that happened, right?
zh: 显然是从 Twitter 到 X 的转变，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: TikTok's almost always been like that.
zh: TikTok 几乎一直就是那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the third way that it's gotten harder is that AI's really good at writing software and code generation, and so everybody's feeling this infinite increase of competition, especially at the startup level.
zh: 然后它变得更难的第三种方式是，AI 非常擅长编写软件和代码生成，所以每个人都感觉到这种竞争的无限增加，尤其是在初创企业层面。

speaker: Unknown
en: YC is pumping out six of the same thing every single cohort.
zh: YC 每一批次都在推出六个相同的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what it literally feels like.
zh: 这就是字面上的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's gotten way harder.
zh: 所以它变得更难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This game, this escape velocity game has gotten a lot harder.
zh: 这场游戏，这个逃逸速度游戏变得难多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's gotten easier in some very exceptional cases like the Cursor or something where AI has been like the spark.
zh: 在一些非常特殊的情况下变得更容易了，比如 Cursor 或其他类似的东西，AI 在那里成为了火花。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you wrote the blog post about the race car engine, and I think you said there's the spark plug in the engine.
zh: 我知道你写了关于赛车引擎的博客文章，我想你说过引擎里有火花塞。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI really created that, a new type of spark, a new type of interest of early adopters to fuel some new players in a short period of time.
zh: AI 真正创造了那一点，一种新的火花，一种早期采用者的新兴趣，在短时间内为一些新参与者提供燃料。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's amazing to see something like Cursor overtake market share of something like GitHub Copilot in nine months or less.
zh: 所以看到像 Cursor 这样的东西在九个月或更短的时间内超过 GitHub Copilot 的市场份额真是太神奇了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's how fast it happens.
zh: 它发生的速度就是这么快。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of crazy.
zh: 这有点疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the main thing that people need to understand is, okay, well, if that's the game I'm playing, how to get to escape velocity before the incumbent?
zh: 但人们需要理解的主要事情是，好吧，如果这是我正在玩的游戏，如何在现有企业之前达到逃逸速度？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are all the ways to do that and to really figure that out?
zh: 有什么方法可以做到这一点并真正弄清楚这一点？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's multiple ways that this can happen, but one of the major ways, one of the major, major ways that we always see is that this can happen when new distribution platforms emerge, because when new distribution platforms emerge, startups are usually the fastest to take advantage of them.
zh: 这种事情有多种发生方式，但主要的方式之一，一种主要的主要方式，我们总是看到的是，当新的渠道平台出现时，这就会发生，因为当新的渠道平台出现时，初创企业通常是最快利用它们的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's slower for the incumbents to move.
zh: 现有企业的行动较慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It gives startups this opportunity essentially to play this game.
zh: 它本质上是给初创企业这个机会来玩这个游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Casey Winters wrote this blog post about two years ago, maybe 18 months ago, about the AI technology shift.
zh: Casey Winters 大约两年前，也许是 18 个月前，写了一篇关于 AI 技术变革的博客文章。

speaker: Unknown
en: His key point was the AI technology shift has been a technology shift that has not come with a distribution shift yet.
zh: 他的关键点是，AI 技术变革是一场尚未伴随渠道变革的技术变革。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look historically, we've had a bunch of technology shifts from the internet to the cloud to mobile to social, all of these different types of things.
zh: 如果回顾历史，我们经历了一系列技术变革，从互联网到云，到移动，到社交，所有这些不同类型的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of them come with new distribution platforms, new ways to distribute products, and some of them don't, but the most powerful ones, the most impactful ones are the ones that do come with these new distribution platforms.
zh: 其中一些伴随着新的渠道平台，分发产品的新方式，一些没有，但最强大的，最有影响力的是那些确实带来这些新渠道平台的。

speaker: Unknown
en: His second key point was that these two things don't actually happen at once.
zh: 他的第二个关键点是，这两件事实际上不会同时发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Usually you get the technology shift, then you get the distribution shift a little bit later.
zh: 通常你会先经历技术转变，然后稍晚一点再经历分发转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we're a couple years from that post.
zh: 现在距离那篇帖子已经有几年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are a couple years into AI technology shift, and one of the things that I am seeing is all of the conditions, all of the ingredients for a new distribution platform to emerge are essentially happening.
zh: 我们进入 AI 技术转变已经几年了，我看到的一件事是，一个新分发平台出现的所有条件、所有要素本质上都在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think we're at an inflection point where we're going to see this emerge really fast.
zh: 所以我认为我们正处于一个拐点，我们将看到它非常快地涌现。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 每个人都需要知道的关键是，随着新分发平台的出现，它们遵循相同的四步周期，这是一个你正在参与的游戏，每个人都在参与。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just like any game, you need to know the rules of the game.
zh: 就像任何游戏一样，你需要知道游戏规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure everybody's seen that AI, we've been calling them the AI manifesto memos from CEOs out there that proclaim, "We are now AI-native," in some grandiose way, but behind the scenes, there's actually some incredibly stark differences in the actual teeth of what backs up those memos and backs up those executive decrees that we should all be AI.
zh: 我确每个人都看到过 AI，我们一直称它们为来自 CEO 的 AI 宣言备忘录，它们以某种宏大的方式宣称，“我们现在就是 AI 原生”，但在幕后，在那些备忘录的实际支持内容和支持这些我们应该都做 AI 的高层法令的实际情况方面，实际上存在一些难以置信的巨大差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just to point out a few of them, which is, one is that I think the most impactful thing that you can do is form really hard constraints.
zh: 指出其中几点，那就是，我认为你可以做的最有影响力的事情是制定真正硬性的约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's other parts that's like, okay, you want to communicate this, you want to establish an owner of who's going to drive this, you want to build an incentives and rewards, and you see this all playing out in things like building it into your career ladders, or some people are starting to introduce this as questions into their performance reviews, all those types of pieces.
zh: 还有其他部分，比如，好吧，你想传达这一点，你想建立一个所有者来驱动这件事，你想建立激励和奖励，你在将其融入你的职业阶梯或有些人开始将其作为问题引入他们的绩效评估等事情中看到所有这些都发挥作用，所有这些类型的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the thing that is actually moving the needle are the companies that are defining incredibly hard constraints.
zh: 但实际上真正起作用的是那些正在定义难以置信的硬性约束的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: One company that we worked with developed this constraint that they benchmarked against other companies of their revenue size and the team sizes for those stages, and they set a benchmark that we will be one-fifth, each of our functions will be one-fifth the size.
zh: 我们与之合作的一家公司制定了这个约束，他们根据收入规模的其他公司和这些阶段的团队规模进行基准比较，他们设定了一个基准，即我们的规模将是五分之一，我们的每个职能的规模将是五分之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: What that did is it created a constraint that you couldn't hire above that level, and it forced people to essentially find ways to adopt AI and do things to replace that.
zh: 这样做的作用是，它创造了一个约束，你不能雇佣超过那个水平的人，它迫使人们本质上寻找方法来采用 AI 并做一些事情来替代它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was one.
zh: 所以那是其中之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've seen these other ones, I can't remember from what company, that might've been Shopify or another, who was like, you are not allowed new headcount until you prove to us that you are not able to accomplish this with AI.
zh: 你见过其他的，我不记得是哪家公司，可能是 Shopify 或另一家，比如，在你向我们证明你无法用 AI 完成这件事之前，你不被允许增加新的人员编制。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's another hard constraint.
zh: 那是另一个硬性约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you also see these other constraints on a smaller level, which is executives saying, "I will not do a product review or review a PRD unless it comes with three prototypes."
zh: 但你也看到这些较小层面的其他约束，即高管说，“除非它附带三个原型，否则我不会做产品审查或审查 PRD。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Something like that.
zh: 诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the hardest one.
zh: 那是最难的一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are the biggest constraints.
zh: 那些是最大的约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the biggest change that I'm seeing is, and the things that separates out the top few percent making this change and everybody else is essentially making the hardest decisions, and that hardest decision is going to come down to exiting people.
zh: 我看到的最大变化是，区分做出这种变革的前百分之几和其他人的东西本质上是在做最艰难的决定，而最艰难的决定归结为让人员离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: In every transformation, what we see is essentially three groups of folks.
zh: 在每一次转型中，我们看到的本质上是三类人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call them the catalysts, the people leading the charge, the people who are experimenting, doing this on their own time, all that kind of stuff.
zh: 我们称他们为催化剂，带头冲锋的人，正在做实验的人，在业余时间做这些事情的人，所有这类东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You then have what we call your converts.
zh: 然后你有我们称之为的皈依者。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are folks that will make the transformation, they will adapt, but they need structure, they need permission, they need a clear outline, they need a clear plan.
zh: 这些人会完成转型，他们会适应，但他们需要结构，他们需要许可，他们需要清晰的大纲，他们需要清晰的计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't say this in a negative way, it's just that that's how some people operate.
zh: 我不是以消极的方式说这句话，这只是有些人就是这样运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's where things like all the things that we were talking about before, which was the decree, the permission, the clear budgets, the rewards, all of those types of things.
zh: 这就是我们之前谈论的所有事情发挥作用的地方，比如法令、许可、明确的预算、奖励，所有这些类型的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then, inevitably you have a certain percentage that are anchors.
zh: 但随后，不可避免地你有一定比例的人是锚。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're dragging their feet, they're silently creating friction in the background and all those pieces.
zh: 他们在拖后腿，他们在幕后默默地制造摩擦，所有这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a big difference in how I think companies are treating and thinking about their strategy for those folks.
zh: 我认为公司在处理和思考针对这些人的策略方面存在很大差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: One group is like, ah, we're going to work with them very passively.
zh: 一组就像，啊，我们将非常被动地与他们合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Others have set a hard deadline.
zh: 其他人都设定了一个硬性截止日期。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're either going to make the transformation by X date or we're going to exit folks.
zh: 他们要么在某个日期前完成转型，要么我们就会让相关人员离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people look at this as being really harsh.
zh: 很多人认为这真的很严厉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of people would think that, especially individuals, but let me explain it from more of a CEO perspective.
zh: 我想很多人会这么认为，尤其是个人，但让我从更多 CEO 的角度来解释一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of these companies are seeing this AI transformation, the ones that are taking it more seriously, as this isn't adopting new tools, this isn't a light change.
zh: 这其中很多公司，那些更认真地对待这种 AI 转型的公司，认为这不是采用新工具，这不是一个轻松的改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a fundamental culture change of how we operate as a company.
zh: 这是我们作为公司运营方式的一种基础文化变革。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't have 20, 30%, whatever meaningful number of it is of your company trying to operate in a completely different way, in a completely different culture.
zh: 你不能让公司里 20%、30%或任何有意义数量的人试图以完全不同的方式、在完全不同的文化中运营。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cultures thrive on density, and that's why there's sometimes the best ones feel like cults.
zh: 文化依赖于密度，这就是为什么有时最好的文化感觉像邪教。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a result, from that perspective, it's like, hey, for us to be successful, for this to be the best thing for all employees, we all need to be operating around the same culture of principles and stuff.
zh: 因此，从这个角度来看，就是，嘿，为了我们要成功，为了这对所有员工来说都是最好的事情，我们所有人都需要围绕相同的文化原则和东西来运营。

speaker: Unknown
en: If that's not you anymore, then we're defining a plan to exit it.
zh: 如果那不再是你的话，那么我们正在制定一个计划让其离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say that less than 10% of companies we see are taking this hard stance, but I would say they are probably the ones that are farthest along getting the most adoption and are seeing the most results of the ones that are taking those hard stances.
zh: 我想说，我们看到的采取这种强硬立场的公司不到 10%，但我想说它们可能是那些进展最远、获得最多采用并且看到了最多结果的公司，在那些采取这种强硬立场的人之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a bunch of other stuff I could talk about, but that's the high level of what we've seen across a bunch of different companies.
zh: 我还可以谈论其他一堆东西，但这就是我们在许多不同公司中看到的高层情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is incredibly interesting.
zh: 这非常有意思。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 第一，如果你是一个正在听这个的 CEO，我会说大多数 CEO 或大多数高管与他们公司内部实际发生的 AI 采用情况极其脱节。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of executives who have done these decrees and all that kind of stuff think it's happening naturally, but we talked to both groups.
zh: 我想很多做过这些法令和所有这类事情的高管认为它正在自然发生，但我们与双方都谈过。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talked to tons of end users and we talked to tons of executives.
zh: 我们与大量的最终用户谈过，我们也与大量的高管谈过。

speaker: Unknown
en: The story we hear from the end users, the PMs, the eng, all that kind of stuff that we talk to using all this stuff, one of the main questions we ask them is, if we're talking to somebody who's picked up a prototyping tool, say, "Well, how many other people on the product and design team are using this?"
zh: 我们从最终用户、PM、eng 以及所有我们交谈的使用所有这些东西的人那里听到的故事，我们要问他们的主要问题之一是，如果我们正在和一个采用原型工具的人交谈，说，『嗯，产品和设计团队里还有多少其他人正在使用这个？』

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost 90% of the time it's like, "Ah, it's me and this one other person," and everybody else hasn't taken it up.
zh: 几乎 90% 的时候都是，『啊，就我和这另一个人』，而其他人还没有采用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a huge disconnect.
zh: 所以存在巨大的脱节。

speaker: Unknown
en: We heard one story, and I can't say the name, but it's a company we all know.
zh: 我们听说了这样一个故事，我不能说出名字，但这是我们都知道的一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a major tech company, a tech-forward company.
zh: 这是一家大型科技公司，一家技术领先的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: CEO's been out there talking about being AI-native.
zh: CEO 一直在那里谈论成为 AI 原生。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talked to one of their principal PMs.
zh: 我们与他们的一位首席 PM 谈过。

speaker: Unknown
en: Person was early to the prototyping tools.
zh: 这个人很早就采用了原型工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: This person shared a prototype with the designer, the eng manager.
zh: 这个人与设计师、eng 经理分享了一个原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: The designer and eng manager escalated it to the VPs.
zh: 设计师和 eng 经理将其上报给了 VP 们。

speaker: Unknown
en: It caused this whole conversation.
zh: 这引发了整个对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Month later, it was still stalling out.
zh: 一个月后，它仍然在停滞。

speaker: Unknown
en: This PM happened to then attend a happy hour where the CEO was at and approached the CEO and told the CEO about the experiment that they were running with prototyping and stuff, and the CEO was like, "This is fantastic.
zh: 这位 PM 碰巧随后参加了一个 CEO 在场的欢乐时光，并走向 CEO 告诉 CEO 关于他们正在用原型和东西进行的实验，CEO 说，『这太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where is it at right now?"
zh: 它现在处于什么阶段？』

speaker: Unknown
en: He was like, "Oh, well, X, Y, Z happened."
zh: 他说，『噢，嗯，X、Y、Z 发生了。』

speaker: Unknown
en: The CEO had no idea.
zh: CEO 完全不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the CEO is like, "Okay, let me take care of it," and then the next day, it happened.
zh: 然后 CEO 说，『好的，让我来处理它』，然后第二天，它就发生了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one is that you have to go to the ground floor on this stuff.
zh: 所以第一点是，你必须深入一线处理这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of the best companies like Shopify and others are measuring actual adoption and usage.
zh: 一些最好的公司像 Shopify 和其他的正在衡量实际的采用和使用情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've gone to the extreme on that front to get a bunch of signals and close to the ground.
zh: 在这方面他们已经走到了极端，以获得大量信号并接近地面。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just goes to show that this is... I don't think we want to talk about going founder mode, but the reality is it's not just about getting into the weeds of your product, but with something this sizable, you got to get into the weeds of the transformation to really understand what's going on and adopt it.
zh: 这只是表明了这一点是... 我想我们不想谈论进入创始人模式，但现实是，这不仅仅是深入你的产品的细节，但对于如此规模的事情，你必须深入转型的细节才能真正理解发生了什么并采用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's point number one.
zh: 这是第一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second point I would say is Fareed, we do this podcast called Unsolicited Feedback, Fareed Mosavat had this great quote on it.
zh: 我要说的第二点是 Fareed，我们做这个叫『Unsolicited Feedback』的播客，Fareed Mosavat 在上面有句很棒的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was like, "Look, your output is constrained by the slowest part of your system."
zh: 他说，『看，你的输出受限于你系统中最慢的部分。』

speaker: Unknown
en: That stuck in my head because it's absolutely true.
zh: 那件事一直印在我脑海里，因为它绝对是正确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about AI adoption as a system, there's all parts of the system that could be slowing adoption.
zh: 如果你把 AI 采用看作一个系统，系统的所有部分都可能正在拖慢采用速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: It might be that people don't feel permission or they don't have the budget or they don't have the knowledge, all these types of things.
zh: 可能是人们觉得没有得到许可，或者他们没有预算，或者他们没有知识，所有这类事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a lot of these cases, it's things like IT, legal, procurement are the slowest part of the friction and are setting the pace of all of this output.
zh: 在很多这类情况下，像 IT、法务、采购这些环节是摩擦中最慢的部分，并正在设定所有这些产出的节奏。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can also see this in just product teams.
zh: 你也可以在产品团队中看到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's been all this talk about product managers are becoming the new bottleneck because engineers are speeding up.
zh: 一直有各种讨论说产品经理正在成为新的瓶颈，因为工程师正在加速。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, that's because people are speeding up one part of the product system and not the other parts, which makes sense.
zh: 嗯，那是因为人们正在加速产品系统的一个部分，而不是其他部分，这是说得通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They adopted all of this tooling for engineers because they're the biggest head count and the most expensive and all that type of stuff, but product is an output of design, PMs, and engineering.
zh: 他们为工程师采用了所有这些工具，因为工程师是最大的人员成本，也是最昂贵的，以及所有这类东西，但产品是设计、PM 和工程的产出。

speaker: Unknown
en: The system is there not to produce code, it's to ship product, and shipping product is the function of those three things.
zh: 系统的存在不是为了生产代码，而是为了交付产品，而交付产品是这三件事的功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you just accelerate one part of the system, you're just going to move to the bottleneck to another part and your actual product output, the output of the system doesn't accelerate, either.
zh: 如果你只是加速系统的一个部分，你只会把瓶颈转移到另一个部分，而你实际的产品产出，即系统的产出也不会加速。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think people have to really understand those two things: what is actually happening on the ground floor, and what is the slowest part?
zh: 我认为人们必须真正理解这两件事：基层实际上正在发生什么，以及最慢的部分是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the thing that is causing the slowest part of the adoption?
zh: 是什么导致了采用过程中最慢的部分？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just attack them ruthlessly if you're really serious about making this transition.
zh: 如果你真的认真对待这种转型，就无情地解决它们。

zh: 我们都习惯的所有这些方式，好吧，这就是我们要做的方式。
